newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates close up, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates close up, seen rising.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed higher on Monday in the aftermath of last week's rupee devaluation and lower estimates of the 1996/97 (July-June) crop.

Dealers attributed the rise to official downward revision of crop estimates to 9.2-9.5 million 375-lb bales from a target of 10 million. Prices had also firmed in response to last Tuesday's 7.86 percent devaluation of the rupee against the dollar.
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 variety was traded at 2,200 rupees per maund plus 10 percent sales tax, the dealer said.
The rate was likely to open higher on Tuesday, he said.
